Seminar Title:

Lead Free Hybrid Metal Halides Containing Sulfur-based Cations: Synthesis, Structure, and Photoluminescence Properties

Seminar Type:

Department:

Speaker Name:

Suman Saptaparna Das ( Rollno : 520cy3001)

Chemistry Seminar Hall

Contact:

Sarojalochan Samal

Abstract:

Metal halides have emerged as a versatile class of optoelectronic materials owing to their structural diversity, tunable electronic and excellent photo-physical properties. Among the metal halides, the lead-based organic inorganic metal halides (OIMH) are thoroughly studied owing to their superior optoelectronic properties, however, the poor stability of these metal halides towards, moisture, air and light and the intrinsic toxicity of lead metal have been of great concern for potential commercial applications. In this thesis, several new low-dimensional, lead-free metal halides containing sulfur-based organic cations are synthesized and their structural luminescence properties are studied with an emphasis on understanding the underlying relationship among these. A series of Bi/Sb based zero- and one-dimensional metal halides was successfully synthesized via facile solution-processed routes, enabling precise control over metal composition, dimensionality, and local coordination environments. Systematic metal substitution and compositional modulation were found to induce pronounced local structural distortions that strongly influence the photoluminescence behavior. Detailed structural and optical analyses reveal the critical role of isolated metal&ndashhalide octahedra and stereochemically active lone pairs on the formation of self-trapped excitons, which in turn result excellent emission efficiency, lifetime, and color purity. The insights gained from this study provide fundamental guidelines for balancing emission color tunability and radiative efficiency in low-dimensional, lead-free metal halides containing sulfur based organic cations, highlighting their potential for future solid-state lighting and optoelectronic applications.
